events.text:
Two books rest side by side on the study desk, beside the diary, leaving the aquarium and its handwritten note undisturbed. Each has a tangible cover, spine, individually turnable pages, and its own weight. Both can be held, opened, closed, and set down.

The larger book is Mary Shelley's Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus, in its original 1818 edition. It is a solid leather-bound tome, 23 cm tall, 15 cm wide and 4.2 cm thick, weighing approximately 950 g. The leather is very dark brown, appearing black except in direct sunlight, where its brown color becomes unmistakable. It is well worn, with softened corners, fine creases and faded gold leaf in the embossed cover lettering. The shallow depressions of the letters and the slightly uneven gold leafing can be felt beneath a fingertip. The cover has a slight scent of leather; the pages carry a very faint scent of parchment, with a faint lavender note intended on approximately 15 percent of separate openings. Inside the front cover, a handwritten inscription in gold ink reads exactly: "To Calibos, To a new world of gods and monsters!" On reaching physical page 86, the far-off sound of a crow cawing can be heard in the distance. At the start of Volume II, Chapter VII, a slight smell of an old fire enters the room, accompanied by the sweet, cloying smell of marshmallows. The moment these scents become noticeable and their origin begins to seem puzzling, they dissipate as quickly as they appeared. These are brief reading-linked sensory occurrences, not present when first discovering the books.

Full-text source (external reference; text not embedded): https://archive.org/download/Frankenstein1818Edition/frank-a5_djvu.txt

The smaller book is The Adventures of Pinocchio by Carlo Collodi, translated by Carol Della Chiesa. It measures 19 cm tall, 13 cm wide and 2.6 cm thick, and weighs approximately 420 g. Its red binding resembles leather but smells faintly more of vinyl than leather. The pages have a subtle dusty scent, as though the book has stood undisturbed on a shelf for quite some time. When the book is opened to its physical page 127, a faint smell of coffee and salt tinges the air, mingling briefly with the usual dusty scent. This particular scent is localized to page 127. At the start of Chapter 35 (XXXV), a faint smell of salt water wafts through the room, then gently fades. An illustration on the front cover shows a wooden marionette in a small carpenter's workshop. A distinct diagonal boundary runs across the illustration: its upper-left triangular half is noticeably bleached by exposure to light, while the remainder retains more color, although it too has faded with age. The inside of the front cover bears a handwritten gold-ink inscription matching the first book: "The creation of life is enthralling, distinctly enthralling, is it not? - J"

Full-text source (external reference; text not embedded): https://www.gutenberg.org/files/500/500-0.txt
